mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.5 percentage points in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates expanding supply capacity, which typically coincides with positive corporate earnings and higher equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the prior 12-month average for four consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
